summary: Re-audit of Phase S3 after remediation round 1 at audited head 2bc7b271 passes. (1) The cb3d1ba1 shared-rule refactor keeps each Red assertion at least as strong: S3 case 1 moved the fallback check from a substring match to exact equality (`script === 'tsc --noEmit'`, stronger than the old `includes`), and case 4 moved its regex to module scope unchanged (`TSC_COMMAND_RE` is the same pattern; only the binding changed). (2) The ddca656c gates.sh fix is correct: `DISK_FULL_RE` (gates.sh:30) is shared by `has_infra_output` and `key()`; my own grep probes confirm the five designed system forms match (libuv ENOSPC/EDQUOT text, `Error: ENOSPC|EDQUOT`, `errno: -28|-122`, `code: ENOSPC|EDQUOT` with or without quotes) while a word-only test title, prose, a file path, `code: EPERM`, and `errno: -13` stay normal diagnostics; the three Red guard cases of 90b31fe0 pass and adv i proves the fix live (word-bearing title yields NEWFAIL, real message yields INFRA and leaves no key). (3) The adv 13 temp folder leaked because probe cleanup runs only in vitest `afterEach`, which a process-level interrupt skips; Green removed it by hand and the corrected r5 log handoff records the truth. (4) The plan round-1 sub-box and the Green r5 log claims match the recorded gates/s3 artifacts. (5) All five suite re-runs in a detached worktree at 2bc7b271 match the claims exactly: gates-script file 19 passed, S3 adversarial 8 passed, S3 tsrs 8 passed, S2 adversarial 13 passed, full scripts suite 80 passed with only the pre-existing remediate-concept-blueprints row failing. Two new nonblocking findings (matcher edge forms, probe-debris sweep) and the four r1 checkpoint items carry forward.
nonblocking_findings: F1 [Minor] review-a: DISK_FULL_RE (measure/tracks/vinext-oxc-toolchain_20261114/gates.sh:30) misses two real disk-full forms that tools in this pipeline can write: the Rust io form `No space left on device (os error 28)` (oxlint and tsrs are Rust binaries) and Node's bare `Error: spawn ENOSPC`. A real disk-full written in either form is classified a new diagnostic (NEWFAIL, exit 1) instead of infrastructure (INFRA, exit 3). Rationale: no hidden pass exists (the job exits non-zero, new_keys reports the line, the gate still fails, and the message stays visible in the log), but the INFRA label and the `GATES_RESUME=1` automatic re-run semantics do not apply, so a true disk event is reported as a code regression. Verified live: my grep probes against the sourced script show nomatch for both forms and match for all five designed forms. Secondary, same bucket: the `code: 'ENOSPC'` alternative means a failing guard test's own output (which quotes the seeded real message) classifies the scripts-suite step as INFRA rather than NEWFAIL; misclassification only, both paths are red.

F2 [Minor] review-a: the oxlint probe folders inside repo apps (`apps/*/.oxlint-adv*`, created by `fs.mkdtempSync` at scripts/__tests__/oxc-toolchain-gates.test.ts:1951, 2009, 2206, 2256, 2315, 2374, 2448) clean up only through the vitest `afterEach` at lines 223-228, which a process-level interrupt (watchdog kill, session stop) skips, and no suite-start sweep of stale folders exists. The first r5 role-gate run failed GREEN on exactly this leak: `apps/integrated-math-3/.oxlint-adv13-49VCiN/` held 14 carrier files the allow-list does not name (r5 log handoff, corrected by 2bc7b271); Green removed it by hand. Rationale: the leak recurs by construction on any killed run and breaks later gate runs; a `beforeAll` sweep of stale `apps/*/.oxlint-adv*`, `apps/*/.oxlint-probe-*`, and root `.oxlint-adv-cfg-*` folders whose mtime predates the current process start would close it without racing a parallel live run. A fresh `.oxlint-adv11-UwbaUm/` folder sat under apps/integrated-math-3 during this audit (a live parallel-session run or a second leak; I did not touch it).

F3 [Minor] review-a (carried from r1 F1 at 5d91443c, unchanged at 2bc7b271, checkpoint item): measure/tech-stack.md S3 note (current lines ~199-201) states a contract the final tree does not hold: the root declares `typescript` `^7.0.2` in devDependencies and in overrides, and bus-math-v2 gets the tsrs app script. At the audited head the root devDependencies hold the `@typescript/native` alias, the overrides block is gone, and bus-math-v2 runs `tsc --noEmit`. Rationale: a reader of tech-stack.md alone gets a wrong current state; the phase checkpoint should add one dated line that names the final state.

F4 [Nit] review-a (carried from r1 F2, unchanged, checkpoint item): measure/tech-debt.md IM3 heap row still says 'The typecheck script carries the heap setting (b9d27742)'. S3 set the IM3 typecheck to plain `tsc --noEmit` on the native tsc 7.0.2 binary, so the Node heap setting is gone. Rationale: the row is stale; close it or annotate it with the S3 change at the checkpoint.

F5 [Nit] review-a (carried from r1 F3, unchanged, checkpoint item): oxc-evidence.md section 9 table rows for IM1, IM3, and PreCalc say tsc 7.0.2 'runs through node_modules/@typescript/native/bin/tsc and reports the pre-existing convex project diagnostics', but a re-run prints only the bundler loader errors for the katex CSS side-effect import. Rationale: the exit code and the pre-existing substance are right; the mechanism sentence is not supported by the output; the keep decision rests on the subset rule, so this is precision only.

F6 [Nit] review-a (carried from r1 F4, unchanged, checkpoint item): oxc-evidence.md section 5 reads the raw after values from `s3-tsrs-raw.txt` (23 workspaces), but the file holds 27 sections: the 23 tsrs runs plus 4 warm-cache `tsc --noEmit` rows (bus-math-v2, IM1, IM3, PreCalc at file lines 1, 11, 21, 26); the four used fallback medians come from `s3-tsc-after-raw.txt`. Rationale: bookkeeping precision; the table medians recompute correctly from the raw files.

The working tree holds the 6 known dirty generated files; a parallel adversarial session has an uncommitted edit to scripts/__tests__/vinext-oxc-gates-script.test.ts in the main checkout, so every suite re-run ran in a detached worktree at 2bc7b271 (removed after).

Refactor strength (item 1): `git diff 5d91443c..cb3d1ba1 -- scripts/__tests__/oxc-toolchain-gates.test.ts` shows case 1 replaced the old `if (!script.includes('tsc --noEmit'))` fallback check with `typecheckScriptFault`, which requires `script === 'tsc --noEmit'` exactly (strictly stronger; `tsc --noEmit --skipLibCheck` and `npx tsc --noEmit` now fail the guard) and keeps the non-fallback exact equality. Case 4 keeps the identical regex `\b(npx\s+(-\S+\s+)*tsc\b|tsc\s+(-p|--project|--noEmit)\b)` as module-scope `TSC_COMMAND_RE`; the loop body and the per-file sentinel are unchanged. adv 1 drives the extracted rule over 17 seeded mutants with a paired control on the 27 real workspaces, and adv 7 drives the shared regex over 7 hidden tsc forms and 4 controls.

DISK_FULL_RE (item 2): gates.sh:30 defines one pattern, gates.sh:35 (`has_infra_output`) and gates.sh:56 (`key`) both use it. Live probes with the sourced script: 'ENOSPC: no space left on device, write', 'EDQUOT: disk quota exceeded', 'Error: ENOSPC: no space left on device, write', 'Error: EDQUOT: disk quota exceeded, write', 'errno: -28', 'errno: -122', 'code: ENOSPC', 'code: EDQUOT' all match; 'FAIL ... handles the ENOSPC write path', '# tsc is gone; ENOSPC is an errno word', 'code: EPERM', 'errno: -13', 'Error: spawn ENOSPC', 'OSError: No space left on device (os error 28)' all stay normal diagnostics. So the fix removes the false-INFRA path the adversarial F1 proved, and the Rust/spawn forms are the residual gap (new F1).

The three Red guard cases of 90b31fe0 (ENOSPC log -> INFRA, EDQUOT log -> INFRA, TS2322 -> NEWFAIL) passed inside the gates-script file run (19 passed). Adv i passed inside the `-t 'S3 adversarial'` run (8 passed): the word-only title is not infra, key() keeps it, new_keys reports it, and a real message is infra and leaves no key. The flipped adv i is a genuine failing-first target: I verified with the sourced old matcher that the pre-fix `grep -qE 'ENOSPC|EDQUOT'` classifies the word-only title as infra, so the new expectations fail against the old script.

adv 13 leak (item 3): the case at oxc-toolchain-gates.test.ts:2437-2449 creates `fs.mkdtempSync(path.join(IM3_DIR, '.oxlint-adv13-'))` and pushes it to `tempDirs`; the `afterEach` at lines 223-228 removes every entry, so an ordinary in-process test failure does clean up. A process-level interrupt skips afterEach; the r5 Green log handoff (corrected by 2bc7b271) records that the first role-gate run failed on the leaked `.oxlint-adv13-49VCiN/` with 14 unlisted carrier files and that Green removed that exact folder. No beforeAll sweep exists (grep for beforeAll/beforeEach in the file finds nothing).
